XIII.|OF THE APOSTLES.|327}}</noinclude>foster-brother of Herod the Tetrarch, and Saul. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=2}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''λειτουργούντων ἀυτῶν''}}∷ {{sup|‖}} as they vvere ministring to our Lord, and fasting, the holy Ghost said: {{sup|‖}} Separate me Saul and Barnabas vnto the vvorke, vvhereto I haue taken them. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=3}}† Then they {{sup|‖}} fasting and praying, and {{sup|‖}} imposing hands vpon them, dimissed them.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=4}}† And they being {{sup|‖}} sent of the holy Ghost, went to Seleucia, and thence sailed to Cypres. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=5}}† And vvhen they vvere come to Salamîna, they preached the vvord of God in the synagogs of the Iewes. And they had Iohn also in their ministerie. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=6}}† And vvhen they had vvalked through out the vvhole iland as farre as Paphos, they found a certaine man that vvas a magician, a false-prophete, a Iew, vvhose name vvas {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`Barieu''}}`Bar-iesu', {{verse|chapter=13|verse=7}}† vvho vvas vvith the Proconsul Sergius Paulus a vvise man. He sending for Barnabas & Saul, desired to heare the vvord of God. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=8}}† But Elymas the magician (for so is his name interpreted) resisted them, seeking to auert the Proconsul from the faith. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=9}}† But Saul, othervvise Paul, replenished vvith the holy Ghost, looking vpon him, {{verse|chapter=13|verse=10}}† said: O ful of al guile, and al deceit, sonne of the deuil, enemie of al iustice, thou ceasest not to subuert the right vvaies of our Lord. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=11}}† And now behold the hand of our Lord vpon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not seing the sunne vntil a time. And forthvvith there fel dimnesse and darkenesse vpon him, and going about he sought some body that vvould giue him his hand. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=12}}† Then the Proconsul, vvhen he had seen that vvhich vvas done, beleeued, marueling at the doctrine of our Lord. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=13}}† And vvhen Paul and they that vvere vvith him had sailed from Paphos, they came to Pergè in Pamphylia. And Iohn departing from them, returned to Hierusalem. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=14}}† But they passing through Pergè, came to Antioche in Pisidia: and entring into the synagogue on the day of the Sabboths, they sate dovvne. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=15}}† And after the lesson of the Lavv and the Prophets, the princes of the Synagogue sent to them, saying, Men brethren, if there be among you any sermon of exhortation to the people, speake. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=16}}† And Paul rising vp, and vvith his hand beckening for<noinclude>{{rh|||silence,}}</noinclude>
